title: Execute lore's Story -> Arc rename: lore-cli's own migration surface
summary: lore-cli execution scope for the fleet-wide Story -> Arc rename decided under OPAG-255 and split for execution under OPAG-277; filed locally so the work exists in this repo's own tracker rather than only opum-agent's (Mechanism C, OPAG-244).
description:
Operator ruling, relayed by opum-agent: lore's "Story" type is renamed to Arc so quest can use "story" as a proper Scrum issue type. Arc was collision-checked clean by lore-cli (zero hits as a CLI verb, profile field, generated schema, or OKF term). Decision record: opum-agent OPAG-255 (closed). Fleet-wide execution split: opum-agent OPAG-277 (To Do).

RULED SEQUENCING (from OPAG-277): this does NOT ride the lore/quest pair release. It is a separate coordinated change that follows it, because it touches published plugin content (needing its own version bump and eval pass), the fleet-wide frontmatter migration script does not exist yet, and profile.strict_types being false everywhere means there is no correctness pressure forcing a flag day.

This task tracks lore-cli's own execution surface only. opum-agent's OPAG-277 tracks fleet coordination and the other repositories' counts; don't treat that record alone as sufficient for this repo's work (Mechanism C, OPAG-244: a design decided by the orchestrator and recorded only in opum-agent/opum-doc doesn't exist from the building repo's own seat until it also lands there).

VERIFIED against dev@928b595a on 2026-09-18 (line numbers are current, not copied from OPAG-277 unread):

1. src/core/profile.ts:965 - the `name: "Story"` schema type entry (single line inside the types array).

2. .lore/schemas/story.schema.json - the generated schema FILENAME changes, so every document's `$schema` frontmatter pointer breaks unless the old name is retained as an alias.

3. src/core/agent-bridge.ts:108,135,156,220 and src/core/codex-bridge.ts:11,37,47,85 hardcode "Story/Task coupling" / "Story <-> Task" into generated skill text that SHIPS IN THE PUBLISHED opum-lore plugin - agent-bridge.ts feeds the Claude skill (`lore instructions`), codex-bridge.ts feeds the Codex skill and AGENTS.md block. Product surface, not internal docs.

4. docs/adr/0009-story-task-coupling-reconciliation.md is LIVE for the Story<->Task naming/coupling decision (only its status-vocabulary section was already superseded by ADR-0022 under LCLI-506); this rename needs its own superseding amendment, not a silent edit of a live ADR.

5. 12 documents under docs/ carry `type: Story` frontmatter and need migrating: docs/adr/0006-schema-types-templates.md, docs/stories/adopt-backlog-knowledge-through-lore.md, docs/stories/build-the-lore-cli-foundation.md, docs/stories/build-the-persistent-local-graph-platform.md, docs/stories/harden-lore-cli-correctness-and-safety.md, docs/stories/harden-post-0-2-lore-correctness.md, docs/stories/hold-deferred-lore-capabilities.md, docs/stories/maintain-lore-cli-documentation-authority.md, docs/stories/prepare-the-first-lore-cli-release.md, docs/stories/retrieve-task-scoped-context-with-agent-profiles.md, docs/stories/support-lore-agent-interoperability.md, docs/stories/track-lore-cli-tracker-backend-integration.md. (lore-spec.md and test/fixtures/okf-bundle/stories/adopt-lore.md also currently match `type: Story` but are spec prose and test fixture content respectively - scope those separately, don't fold them into this count.)

6. `lore rename` alone doesn't perform this migration - it repoints concept ids and links, not a document's `type:` frontmatter value. The fleet-wide frontmatter migration script referenced in OPAG-277 doesn't exist yet; that's a fleet gap, not something specific to this repo to build alone.

FLEET CONSTRAINT while this is open: don't set `profile.strict_types = true` in this repo (or any repo) until the migration completes. Checked 2026-09-18: this repo's .lore/config.toml has no `strict_types` key, i.e. it's already at the required false/unset value - this task only needs to keep it that way, not change anything, until the migration lands.

acceptanceCriteria.text: src/core/profile.ts's name: "Story" entry is renamed to name: "Arc" (or whatever term the fleet-wide decision settles on beyond OPAG-255, if it changes before execution)
.lore/schemas/story.schema.json is renamed/regenerated under the new type name, and every existing document with an old $schema pointer still resolves (alias or rewrite - decide and record which)

Generated skill text in src/core/agent-bridge.ts and src/core/codex-bridge.ts (all 8 occurrences at 108,135,156,220 and 11,37,47,85) says Arc/Task rather than Story/Task, and the regenerated Claude + Codex skill docs are byte-identical on a no-op re-run
docs/adr/0009-story-task-coupling-reconciliation.md carries a superseding amendment recording the Arc rename, following this repo's ADR immutability convention - not a silent edit of the live text
All 12 verified docs/ files carrying type: Story frontmatter are migrated to the new type value via the fleet-wide migration script once it exists
lore check exits 0 on the fully migrated tree, with profile.strict_types left at its current unset/false value for the duration of the fleet-wide migration

implementationNotes:
SCOPE MEASURED ON DISPATCH (opum-agent OPAG-277, read by git archive from its origin/main d5502b2 into scratch, not its working tree). Measured against this branch cut from origin/dev @ 85174242, 2026-09-19.

CORRECTION TO THIS RECORD AND TO OPAG-277 — THE POINTER IS NOT FRONTMATTER. Both records say the generated schema filename change breaks "every document's $schema FRONTMATTER pointer". It is not frontmatter. NO document carries a $schema frontmatter key at all: the frontmatter key set across the 74 docs/ files that have frontmatter is type(74) title(74) timestamp(74) summary(74) tags(69) description(36) status(14) tasks(11) supersedes(2) superseded_by(2) okf_version(1) — measured by key presence, not by value. The pointer is a LINE-1 EDITOR MODELINE comment, "# yaml-language-server: $schema=../../.lore/schemas/<slug>.schema.json" (ADR-0006 §3), emitted by schema.ts:644 and spliced on serialize by concept.ts:404. I wrote the wrong location into my own record; the substance (a pointer that dangles after the rename) survives, its blast radius does not — an editor modeline degrades editor autocomplete, it does not fail a gate.

NOTHING CATCHES THE DANGLING MODELINE. schemaDriftFindings (check.ts) has exactly three conditions — stale, missing, orphaned — all about the SCHEMA FILES under .lore/schemas/, and a committed of null yields no findings at all. No code anywhere validates that a modeline TARGET resolves; the only yaml-language-server hits in src/ are the two emitters and prose. So after the rename, lore check correctly reports story.schema.json orphaned + arc.schema.json missing, and says nothing about the N documents now pointing at a deleted file. That gap is worth closing as part of this work rather than documenting.

THE DEGRADATION STORY IS VERIFIED IN THE CONSUMING CODE, NOT THE CONFIG COMMENT. validate.ts:151 — severity is "error" only when isUnknownType && effective.strictTypes, otherwise "warning". profile.ts:394 defaults strict_types to false and profile.ts:943 records that the built-in profile never opts in on a project's behalf. So an un-migrated "type: Story" document warns. That is what makes this incremental rather than a flag day, and it is now read from the reader rather than assumed from scaffold.ts's comment.

THE NAME IS NOT A BEHAVIOURAL KEY — WHICH DECIDES THE SHAPE. Literal "Story" in src/ excluding tests is THREE sites, and only three: template.ts:460 (STORY_TEMPLATE const), template.ts:501 (the Story key in BUILTIN_TEMPLATES), and profile.ts:965 (the type declaration). Critically, lore link does NOT key on the type name — link.ts:906 keys on "a concept type whose profile schema declares tasks (the built-in Story type)", a STRUCTURAL predicate; the parenthetical is prose. The renamed Arc type carries the same tasks field, so Story<->Task coupling is a property of the field, not the name. NOT YET MEASURED, and it is the next thing to measure because it decides per-repo migration urgency: whether link still resolves a document whose OWN type is unknown (un-migrated) — an unknown-type document has no profile type, so it plausibly has no declared tasks either.

THE POPULATION IS UNBOUNDED, SO "WHICH DIRECTORIES ARE IN SCOPE" IS THE WRONG FRAME. opum-agent reports lore initialised in 35 directories on this machine, 10 being the tracked fleet, and asks whether the other 25 are in scope. My own sweep of /Volumes/external + ~ (81 config.toml files READ, reported as a count so an empty result could not read as a clean one) finds 81 lore workspaces: 80 carry .lore/schemas/story.schema.json and 46 carry at least one "type: Story" document. But the number is not the point and neither is 35 vs 81 — @opum-ai/lore 0.8.0 is PUBLIC ON NPM (dist-tags.latest = 0.8.0, re-resolved today). Every external user has a story.schema.json and Story documents, and no script run over enumerated directories can ever reach them. The proof that enumeration fails is already on this disk: 15 opum-workflow plugin version caches and 3 opum-lore caches each carry story.schema.json and Story docs. Those are PUBLISHED PAYLOADS ALREADY DISTRIBUTED, frozen at their version — nobody would put them on a migration list and nothing should rewrite them.

SO: the 25 are NOT in scope as migration targets, and neither are the other 45. What is in scope is making the CLI not break them. RECOMMENDED SHAPE, mine to decide per OPAG-277: alias-first, migrate-later — retain Story as a deprecated alias of Arc so existing documents keep validating and external users never see a break, then migrate the 10 fleet repos on their own schedule, and only then may a repo flip strict_types. THE HONEST PRICE, verified: there is NO alias concept in the type system today — zero hits for "alias" in profile.ts, type-vocabulary.ts and schema.ts. This is net-new capability, not a config line, and it is the part worth arguing before committing.

OPAG-277 OPEN GAP CLOSED. It records five repos never counted and 48 as a floor that must not be quoted as a total. Counted here: lore-web 3, quest-web 3, opum-web 0, opum-marketplace 0, opum-fleet 1. OBJECT-IDENTITY CAVEAT, which is why these must be re-resolved before anyone quotes a fleet total: OPAG-277 counted on each repo's origin/dev, mine are WORKING TREES and whole-repo including fixtures and .repro-scratch — which is exactly why this repo reads 23 raw here against the 12 real docs this record already carries. Same basis for all five new numbers; different basis from OPAG-277's.

FEDERATION CONSEQUENCE TO ROUTE. skills/lore/SKILL.md carries 3 Story mentions, and opum-marketplace federates skills/ BY TAG against a recorded tree baseline (pinned v0.7.0, skills/ baseline 2998f74d, per this repo's CLAUDE.md). The rename changes what the next tag ships, so the LCLI-469 handshake applies. And the SKILL.md description line is the skill TRIGGERING description — changing "Story/Task coupling" to "Arc/Task coupling" changes trigger wording, which is precisely what OPAG-277's required eval pass is testing. The 8 bridge sites this record already lists were re-verified unchanged: agent-bridge.ts 108,135,156,220 and codex-bridge.ts 11,37,47,85.
